# agents v0.7.0 — scaffolding, wiring, and the guard

A deliberate reduction. The tool did five jobs; this release keeps three and
deletes the rest rather than maintaining them at a size nobody was reading. It
still scaffolds a repository's context tree, still manages the harness wiring
around it, and still guards the commit message. It no longer records, indexes,
or migrates anything, and it no longer has an opinion about where a
repository's documentation lives.

The measured change: 17 internal packages to 9, and roughly 13,400 non-test
lines to 4,400. Nothing was renamed to hide a deletion.

## Read this before you upgrade

**Run `agents wire` after upgrading, in every repository that wired a harness.**
This is not cleanup you can defer: until you do it, every harness session in
those repositories reports a hook error.

**Getting it from Homebrew works as it always has.** The release workflow
repoints `nilbot/homebrew-tap` at this version as its last step, so
`brew upgrade agents` delivers v0.7.0 once that step has run. It asserts the
result afterwards, so a release whose tap update failed fails loudly instead of
leaving `brew` on the previous version.

`agents` only answers its own subcommands. The git-hook entry points
(`commit-msg`, `pre-commit`, `post-merge`, `post-checkout`) are reached by the
name the binary is invoked under, not by an argument, so a v0.6.0-written
`.claude/settings.json` entry of the form

```
/opt/homebrew/bin/agents hook stop --harness claude-code
```

is an argv whose first word after the binary is `hook`. v0.7.0 has no `hook`
command, so that entry now exits 3 with `unknown command "hook"` and prints the
usage block. Measured directly against the v0.7.0 binary.

Claude Code treats a non-zero exit other than 2 as a **non-blocking** error: the
action proceeds, and the transcript shows a `hook error` notice carrying the
first line of stderr. So your sessions keep working, and the four lifecycle
hooks v0.6.0 installed — session start, stop, subagent start, subagent stop —
each fail loudly with a usage dump until the entries are gone. Nothing records
anything either way, because v0.7.0 records nothing.

There is no migration command. `agents migrate`, `agents layout migrate`, and
`agents update --all` are all gone, and the skill that used to drive a migration
is archived. An upgrade has exactly one follow-up step, per repository:

```bash
agents doctor    # exits 1, naming every entry this version no longer answers
agents wire      # removes them
```

`doctor` reports the retired entries as `FAIL wiring:<harness>` with the remedy
`run agents wire`, per harness. Measured on a v0.6.0-provisioned repository
under v0.7.0: 4 retired entries for claude-code, 4 for codex, 1 for
antigravity. `wire` then removes the three config files, which is the designed
outcome — each held only this tool's entries. A config holding anything else
keeps that content, and a foreign hook in the same file survives untouched.

There is no useful pre-upgrade step. Measured: a v0.6.0 `doctor` does not
mention the entries v0.7.0 will strand, so the cleanup can only happen after the
new binary is on `PATH`.

## What was removed

| Removed | Was for |
|---|---|
| `agents trace ls\|show\|cache\|migrate` | a session record nothing had queried in over a month |
| `agents drift [--json]` | router and skill drift reporting |
| `agents ls [--prune]` | the machine-wide fleet registry |
| `agents save` | committing `.agents/` paths and nothing else |
| `agents update --all [--apply]` | rewiring every registered repository |
| `agents layout show\|validate\|path\|migrate` | resolving and migrating `agents.layout/v2` |

The manifest at `.agents/layout.json` is no longer read. A repository that has
one is not broken by this release — the file is inert, and nothing rewrites or
deletes it. The four documentation roles it resolved (`design`, `plans`,
`journal`, `qna`) remain the layout this tool scaffolds, at `docs/`. A
repository that had migrated its stores elsewhere keeps working as a
repository; `agents` simply stops being the thing that knows the mapping.

`DriftReport` and its JSON shapes are gone with the command that printed them.
This supersedes the v0.6.0 note that deprecated `DriftReport.docs_stores` for
removal no earlier than v0.8.0: the whole structure left one release sooner,
because the reader did too.

## What did not change

- **The exit code table.** All six codes, 0 through 5, are byte-identical to
  v0.6.0. A script that branches on `2` meaning "block" still reads correctly.
- **`agents init`.** It still creates `.agents/`, the four `docs/` stores, the
  root `AGENTS.md` with its `CLAUDE.md` symlink, and the bundled skill. Its
  exit code on a fresh repository is unchanged.
- **The git-hook entry points.** `pre-commit`, `commit-msg`, `post-merge`, and
  `post-checkout` are installed and dispatched exactly as before, and a chain
  installed by `git/install-hooks.sh` keeps working across a binary swap. This
  is separate from the retired `agents hook …` *argv* entries the harness
  configs carry: those are commands, not entry points, and they are what
  `wire` removes.
- **The commit-message guard.** `commit-msg` still strips AI attribution
  footers, and still matches both documented URL forms
  (`https://claude.ai/code` and `https://claude.com/claude-code`) plus the
  `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer.
- **The bundled skill.** `recording-what-you-learn` is still installed and is
  the only skill this tool now carries.

## The `migrating-fleet-context` skill is archived

The skill that used to drive a layout migration taught `agents drift`, `agents
update --all --apply`, and `agents layout migrate`. Every one of those commands
is gone, so the skill is dead text and is no longer installed or verified. It
is kept in the archive as the record of how the migration worked, not as
instructions to follow. `## Follow-up` work in the archived design notes is
likewise historical.

## Measured fleet baseline

Read-only, before and after the reduction, on this machine: no repository
carried a `drift` or `layout` state that this release changes. One repository
held retired hook entries; `agents wire` removed them and `doctor` then
reported clean. The upgrade is a no-op for a repository that never wired a
harness, which is what `wire` now does there: nothing.

## `wire` removes entries; it no longer writes any

This is the one behavioural change to internalize. A v0.6.0 `wire` merged this
tool's hook entries into `.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, and
`.agents/hooks.json`, creating each file. A v0.7.0 `wire` does the opposite: it
removes this tool's entries and writes nothing back.

On a repository that never had any, it therefore changes no config at all. What
it does leave is the `.claude/skills` and `.codex/skills` symlinks to
`.agents/skills`, and a `.agents-wire.lock` file per harness directory — the
lock is held with `flock` for the duration of the run and is deliberately not
unlinked, so its presence afterwards is not a failure.
